d3300.Raw_Article: 3300 Ta. tuṭum-eṉal onom. expr. signifying jumping sound, as into water. Ka. duḍuṃ, duḍhuṃ imitation of the sound of a body suddenly falling or plunging into water; duḍhum ir̤i to plunge. Kol. duḍm- (duḍumt-) to swim. DED 2702.

d5058.Raw_Article: 5058 Ta. meṭṭu mound, heap of earth; mēṭu height, eminence, hillock; muṭṭu rising ground, high ground, heap. Ma. mēṭu rising ground, hillock; māṭu hillock, raised ground; miṭṭāl rising ground, an alluvial bank; (Tiyya) maṭṭa hill. Ka. mēḍu height, rising ground, hillock; miṭṭu rising or high ground, hill; miṭṭe state of being high, rising ground, hill, mass, a large number; (Hav.) muṭṭe heap (as of straw). Tu. miṭṭè prominent, protruding; muṭṭe heap. Te. meṭṭa raised or high ground, hill; (K.) meṭṭu mound; miṭṭa high ground, hillock, mound; high, elevated, raised, projecting; ( VPK ) mēṭu, mēṭa, mēṭi stack of hay; (Inscr.) meṇṭa-cēnu dry field (cf. meṭṭu-nēla, meṭṭu-vari ). Kol. (SR.) meṭṭā hill; (Kin.) meṭṭ , (Hislop) met mountain. Nk. meṭṭ hill, mountain. Ga. (S. 3 , LSB 20.3) meṭṭa high land. Go. (Tr. W. Ph.) maṭṭā , (Mu.) maṭṭa mountain; (M. L.) meṭā id., hill; (A. D. Ko.) meṭṭa , (Y. Ma. M.) meṭa hill; (SR.) meṭṭā hillock ( Voc. 2949). Konḍa meṭa id. Kuwi (S.) metta hill; (Isr.) meṭa sand hill. Cf. 5474 Ta. viṭam. DED(S, N) 4151.
